feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report whether line_loss_events stayed at 0 with the ±0.06 span. Report max_error on each track and whether it dropped below about 0.055 compared with the 0.061 floor in iteration 2. Say whether the robot shows a steady lean to one side (a bias that kp alone cannot remove), which would point to the motor mismatch. Say whether 0.12 m track gave enough turn authority on the s-bend and slalom, and whether slalom steering_oscillation stayed below about 0.15.

intent: Keep the ±0.06 m sensor span that removed line losses, and widen the drive track from 0.10 to 0.12 m. The aim is to reduce the mismatch-driven drift that pins max_error at about 0.061 on every track, so the robot stays on the line through the bends and progresses past the first bend on oval and s-bend.
learning: Line losses are fixed by the ±0.06 span, so the remaining off-track failure is not a sensing gap. Oval progress was 0.115 in all three designs, and max_error sat at 0.061 regardless of span, track, or lookahead. That points to a steady drift from the fixed motor mismatch, which geometry can reduce mainly through wheel_track. If wheel_track 0.12 does not lower max_error, the next test is wheel_track 0.14 or wheel_radius changes, and the controller side should consider ki.
rationale: Iteration 2 widened the outer sensors to ±0.06 m. Line-loss events fell from 1 to 0 on all tracks, which confirms the span was limiting sensing. But the robot still left the track at max_error 0.0609 to 0.0614, the same floor as before, and slalom progress dropped from 0.105 to 0.035. Oval progress stayed at 0.115 across all three designs, so the failure point is not driven by sensing. Since every design leaves at about 0.061 m, the likely cause is a steady drift. The fixed left/right motor mismatch in the simulator produces a yaw rate that scales inversely with wheel_track, because turn rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by track. A wider track therefore lowers the drift for the same mismatch. Body width cannot help: the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for any body up to about 0.19 m. I keep the ±0.06 span and 16 mm footprints, since they removed the line losses, and keep y = 0.03 to limit lag. I change only wheel_track, from 0.10 to 0.12 m, as the Integrator's requested next step. Expected result: line losses stay at 0, and max_error on bends drops below about 0.055 if mismatch drift is the cause. If max_error does not move, drift is not from track width, and the next test should be ki or a wider track (0.14 m). Slalom oscillation should stay near 0.15 or below, so the controller has room.
